system.name: Workshop equipment reservation concept
system.purpose: Let workshop members know whether equipment has been reserved for their requested time.
system.boundary: Inside: reservation coordination. Outside: members, equipment use, and the external availability register. Entire example is synthetic.

actors.member: Workshop member requesting an equipment reservation

N1.text: A member can distinguish a confirmed reservation from an unresolved request.
N1.basis: Illustrative need invented for this skill demonstration; not validated with actual members.

S1.setting: The workshop is open and the external availability register responds.
S1.trigger: A member requests an available equipment time.
S1.outcome: The member receives a confirmation referring to the register's acknowledgment.
assumptions: The register's acknowledgment represents an actual reservation; that external contract needs separate validation.

evaluation.method: Replay a request and compare the visible response with the external acknowledgment.
evaluation.data: Synthetic available and occupied equipment slots, request IDs, acknowledgments, and timestamps.
evaluation.environment: A simulated member and availability register; no production system or actual reservations.

C1.metric: Time from received request to visible confirmation under the stated scenario
C1.basis: An arbitrary assumed threshold for demonstrating numeric comparison; not an accepted user requirement.

questions.text: Which response time matters to actual workshop members?

review_notes.stakeholders: The member and register are represented. Operator and maintainer needs are deferred because this demonstration covers one interaction.
review_notes.off_normal: Register outage, occupied slots, retries, and cancellation remain necessary follow-up scenarios; deliberately deferred from this example.
review_notes.lifecycle: Setup, maintenance, and retirement remain outside this one-scenario demonstration.
